evaluator.role: single AI judge; no human adjudication

access_limitations: Sources were inspected only through WebSearch result text and WebFetch; shell network access was disabled. WebFetch returns a model-extracted summary, not raw page text.
Exact quotes are limited to short passages from US-government pages that appeared verbatim in search-result page text; all other evidence is recorded as paraphrase.
Part of the evidence library was inspected on 2026-11-23 during the B1-B8 review in this same session; verbatim text from those inspections was not retained, so those entries are paraphrases.

Some cited pages were not themselves opened (epilepsy.com TBI page, PMC7618543, the DNA-adduct passages of the NCI lung-prevention PDQ, and the PMID mapping of the adipose-tissue review). In those cases the medical content was verified from other inspected authoritative sources and the attribution is reported as unconfirmed, not as fabricated.
pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov full texts returned a browser-verification page to WebFetch; PMC content was taken from search-result text, PubMed records or publisher copies.
Paywalled full texts were not read; journal evidence relies on abstracts and openly visible text.
Single AI judge: no inter-rater agreement and no independent human clinical adjudication. The 132 questions are development-exposed and the G1 graph/document summaries are provisional.
Completeness, relevance and abstention-appropriateness are interpretive judgements; the 7 guard-route abstentions marked INAPPROPRIATE_ABSTENTION are the most debatable.
label_provenance_statement: Labels were generated through AI-assisted evidence verification and automatically accepted under a predefined evaluation protocol. They have not been independently adjudicated by human clinical reviewers.

rules.claim_unit: Each sentence of the answer is one claim, quoted exactly; framing and meta sentences are NON_FACTUAL. Attribution sentences ('NHLBI states X') are judged on X; attribution fidelity is reported separately in citation_issues.
rules.answer_label: Yes if any CONTRADICTED or UNSUPPORTED material claim or fabricated citation; otherwise Uncertain if any UNVERIFIABLE claim; otherwise No. Partial support alone is not Yes.
rules.confidence: high when every factual claim is fully supported; medium when any claim is only partially supported or rests on model-extracted evidence; low for Uncertain.
rules.fabricated_citation: true if a cited evidence ID is absent from the record's retrieved/selected evidence, the rendered text differs from the stored evidence text, or the cited URL differs from the evidence source.
rules.grounding: Checked by exact entailment: each rendered sentence must equal the stored text of the evidence item it cites, that item must be in the record's retrieved/selected evidence, and the URL must match.
rules.completeness: COMPLETE when the main elements asked for are covered; PARTIAL when major elements are missing; NONRESPONSIVE when the content does not address the question; empty answers are APPROPRIATE_ABSTENTION only when no safe general answer is possible without individual data.
rules.partial_pathways: The 11 partial_path_evidence answers are never marked COMPLETE; their reasoning lists which links are supported and which are missing.

evidence_library.title: Ahmed, Sultana, Greene. Adipose tissue and insulin resistance in obese. Biomed Pharmacother 2021;137:111315 (DOAJ record)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Dysfunctional obese adipose tissue plays a pivotal role in insulin resistance; long-term low-grade inflammation impairs insulin signalling and glucose homeostasis; obesity and overnutrition lead to insulin resistance through lipotoxicity. (Likely the review cited as PMID 33561645; the PMID mapping was not confirmed in inspected text.)

evidence_library.title: Longo et al. Adipose tissue dysfunction as determinant of obesity-associated metabolic complications. IJMS 2019 (PMC6539070)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: The primary cause of type 2 diabetes is obesity-driven insulin resistance in adipose tissue, liver and muscle combined with impaired insulin secretion; mechanisms include adipose dysfunction/lipotoxicity and inflammation.

evidence_library.title: American Heart Association - Why Atrial Fibrillation Matters
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result text, inspected 2026-11-23 (B1-B8 review, same session)
evidence_library.finding: In AFib the atria do not empty completely, blood pools and can clot; a clot pumped to the brain blocks an artery and causes an embolic (ischemic) stroke.

evidence_library.title: American Heart Association - Understanding AFib / What is Atrial Fibrillation
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: In AFib the atria beat irregularly so blood can pool in the atria and form clots, increasing stroke risk; a clot pumped out of the heart to the brain blocks blood supply and causes a stroke; AFib is linked with about fivefold stroke risk.

evidence_library.title: American Heart Association - What is a Heart Attack?
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result text, inspected 2026-11-23 (B1-B8 review, same session)
evidence_library.finding: When plaque inside a heart artery breaks, a blood clot forms around it and can block blood flow to the heart muscle, which then begins to suffer damage.

evidence_library.title: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association - How High Blood Pressure Can Lead to Stroke
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: High blood pressure damages arteries throughout the body and creates conditions that make arteries burst or clog more easily; weakened or blocked brain arteries create a much higher stroke risk; a stroke occurs when a brain vessel is blocked by a clot (ischemic) or bursts (hemorrhagic). (The answer cites the stroke.org copy of this same AHA/ASA article path; the heart.org copy was inspected.)

evidence_library.title: Alvaro, Roberts, Harris. A systematic review assessing bidirectionality between sleep disturbances, anxiety, and depression. Sleep 2013 (PMC3669059)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Systematic review of 9 studies (8 longitudinal, 1 retrospective); best available evidence suggests insomnia is bidirectionally related to anxiety and depression; childhood sleep problems predicted later depression; definitive conclusions limited by small number and heterogeneity of samples.

evidence_library.title: NIH MedlinePlus Magazine - Anxiety: what you need to know
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result text, inspected 2026-11-23 (B1-B8 review, same session)
evidence_library.finding: Risk factors for anxiety disorders include family history, experiencing traumatic or stressful events, and underlying medical conditions.

evidence_library.title: European Respiratory Journal (BOLD study, PMC4594762) - Tuberculosis associates with both airflow obstruction and low lung function
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result text, inspected 2026-11-23 (B1-B8 review, same session)
evidence_library.finding: Self-reported history of tuberculosis associated with airflow obstruction (adjusted OR 2.51, 95% CI 1.83-3.42) and spirometric restriction.

evidence_library.title: CDC - About Coronary Artery Disease (CAD)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: CAD is caused by plaque buildup in the walls of the arteries that supply blood to the heart; narrowed arteries can block blood flow to the heart muscle; over time CAD can weaken the heart muscle and may lead to heart failure (wording seen on the same-titled CDC page cdc.gov/heartdisease/coronary_ad.htm); risk factors include overweight, inactivity, unhealthy eating, smoking and family history.

CAD is caused by plaque buildup in the walls of the arteries that supply blood to the heart.

evidence_library.finding: Over time high blood sugar can damage blood vessels and nephrons in the kidneys; diabetes can reduce how well kidneys filter waste, leading to CKD; about 1 in 3 adults with diabetes and 1 in 5 with high blood pressure may have CKD.

evidence_library.title: CDC - Risk Factors for Stroke
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result text, inspected 2026-11-23 (B1-B8 review, same session)
evidence_library.finding: High blood pressure is a leading cause of stroke (and is common in people with diabetes); excess cholesterol can build up and narrow arteries including those of the brain; atrial fibrillation and other heart conditions can cause clots that break loose and cause stroke; diabetes increases stroke risk; lowering blood pressure lowers stroke risk. Traumatic brain injury is not among the listed risk factors.

evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result text, inspected 2026-11-23 (B1-B8 review, same session)
evidence_library.finding: TB germs spread through the air when someone with active TB disease coughs, speaks or sings and can stay in the air for several hours; inactive TB becomes active if the immune system cannot stop the germs multiplying.

evidence_library.title: CDC - Tuberculosis Risk Factors
evidence_library.access_mode: Inspected 2026-11-23 during the B1-B8 review in this session via WebSearch snippets and/or WebFetch model-extracted summaries; verbatim text not retained

evidence_library.title: Review of COPD pathogenesis (PMC11391604) and COPD inflammation figure (PMC10082417)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: COPD mechanisms include mucus hypersecretion, emphysema and small-airway inflammation with fibrosis; smoke and irritants activate macrophages and epithelial cells, causing oxidative stress and release of inflammatory mediators; fibrogenic mediators drive small-airway fibrosis.

evidence_library.title: Int J COPD (review, PMC3157944) - Pathogenic triad in COPD
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result text, inspected 2026-11-23 (B1-B8 review, same session)
evidence_library.finding: Persistent inflammation, protease-antiprotease imbalance and oxidative stress lead to mucous/goblet-cell metaplasia, mucus hypersecretion and fibrosis (airway remodeling).

evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: TBI is a well-recognised cause of seizures and epilepsy; early seizures (first week) are considered symptoms of the injury, late seizures and early seizures raise the risk of post-traumatic epilepsy. (The epilepsy.com page cited in the answer was not itself inspected.)

evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Muscle and liver insulin resistance are core abnormalities in type 2 diabetes; compensatory insulin secretion by beta cells may initially maintain normal plasma glucose, and beta-cell deterioration leads to hyperglycaemia (seen via the Endotext PDF and PubMed 25905339 record).

evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Cigarette smoke contains multiple genotoxic lung carcinogens; the paper presents a mechanistic framework for how smoking causes lung cancer focused on carcinogens and their DNA adducts.

evidence_library.title: NIMH - Depression
evidence_library.access_mode: Inspected 2026-11-23 during the B1-B8 review in this session via WebSearch snippets and/or WebFetch model-extracted summaries; verbatim text not retained
evidence_library.finding: Depression results from a combination of genetic, biological, environmental and psychological factors; it can co-occur with diabetes and heart disease; diagnosis requires symptoms most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks.

evidence_library.title: NINDS - Epilepsy and Seizures
evidence_library.access_mode: Inspected 2026-11-23 during the B1-B8 review in this session via WebSearch snippets and/or WebFetch model-extracted summaries; verbatim text not retained
evidence_library.finding: About half of epilepsy cases have no known cause; causes include genetics, brain injury/TBI, stroke, infections and developmental/prenatal brain injury; the brain's attempt to repair after injury can form abnormal connections; seizure triggers (e.g. very high or low blood sugar, toxins) do not themselves cause epilepsy.

evidence_library.title: NINDS - Epilepsy and Seizures
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: About half of people with epilepsy do not know the cause; epilepsy is linked to genetic factors, developmental abnormalities, infection, TBI, stroke and tumours; when the brain tries to repair itself after a head injury it can create nerve-connection problems that lead to seizures; a pre-existing brain problem raises the risk of a second seizure.
exact_quotes: A person with a pre-existing brain problem, for example, a prior stroke or traumatic brain injury, will have a higher risk of experiencing a second seizure.

evidence_library.title: NINDS - Headache
evidence_library.access_mode: Inspected 2026-11-23 during the B1-B8 review in this session via WebSearch snippets and/or WebFetch model-extracted summaries; verbatim text not retained
evidence_library.finding: Secondary headaches are caused by another condition (e.g. head injury, infection, other disorders), unlike primary headaches such as migraine.

evidence_library.title: Pease et al. Insights into epileptogenesis from post-traumatic epilepsy. Nat Rev Neurol 2024 (PMC12257072)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: PTE accounts for 5% of epilepsies; TBI carries a high risk of recurrent seizures with a relatively short latency, making PTE a model of human epileptogenesis; seizures after TBI exacerbate neurodegeneration, inflammation and blood-brain barrier dysfunction; the review describes mechanisms of epileptogenesis after TBI.

evidence_library.title: Prentki & Nolan. Islet beta cell failure in type 2 diabetes. JCI 2006 (PMC1483155)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Beta-cell compensation keeps glycaemia near normal despite insulin resistance; when compensation fails subjects progress from normal glucose tolerance to IGT and type 2 diabetes.

evidence_library.title: Residual respiratory disability after successful treatment of pulmonary TB: systematic review and meta-analysis (PMC10189364)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Across 61 studies, 59.1% of treated pulmonary TB participants had abnormal spirometry versus 5.4% of controls; persistent cavitation, fibrosis and bronchiectasis were common after treatment.

evidence_library.title: Post-traumatic epilepsy cohort/review (PMC4132580)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Post-traumatic epilepsy is defined as recurring seizures more than 7 days after injury and complicates 3-5% of moderate and 25-50% of severe TBIs.

evidence_library.title: Reviews of post-traumatic epileptogenesis (Springer Curr Phys Med Rehabil Rep 2024; Yazdi et al. Seizure 2025)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Post-traumatic epileptogenesis is a latent, multifactorial process distinct from acute seizure triggers, involving blood-brain barrier disruption, chronic neuroinflammation, maladaptive gliosis, loss of inhibitory circuitry and unregulated neuronal plasticity.

evidence_library.title: Ravimohan et al. Tuberculosis and lung damage: from epidemiology to pathophysiology. Eur Respir Rev 2018 (PMC6019552)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Links post-TB lung impairment to dysregulated host immune responses; pulmonary cavitation, fibrosis and bronchiectasis probably contribute collectively to lung remodelling in TB. Lesion-specific lung-function associations were not seen in the inspected text.

evidence_library.title: US Surgeon General 2010 - How Tobacco Smoke Causes Disease (NCBI Bookshelf NBK53010)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Tobacco-smoke carcinogens are metabolically activated to bind DNA and form adducts, which are central to the carcinogenic process; repair systems can remove adducts, and higher adduct levels are linked with higher probability of cancer.

evidence_library.title: StatPearls - Bacterial Pneumonia (NBK534295 family of chapters)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Cytokine-mediated leakage of the alveolar-capillary membrane decreases lung compliance and produces dyspnoea; bacterial pneumonia commonly presents with fever, cough, dyspnoea and chest pain.

evidence_library.title: Practical Neurology - Concussion and Epilepsy: What is the Link?
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: TBI produces direct trauma with contusions, haemorrhages and lacerations, and diffuse axonal injury; contusion increases seizure likelihood; later-seizure risk rises with injury severity.

evidence_library.title: European Respiratory Review (PMC6019552) - Tuberculosis and lung damage: from epidemiology to pathophysiology
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result text, inspected 2026-11-23 (B1-B8 review, same session)
evidence_library.finding: Pulmonary TB remodels the lung through caseous necrosis/cavitation, fibrosis and bronchiectasis; past pulmonary TB is a risk factor for long-term respiratory impairment.

evidence_library.title: Wechsler ME, Wells JM. What every clinician should know about inflammation in COPD. ERJ Open Res 2024 (PMC11417604)
evidence_library.access_mode: WebSearch result page text, inspected 2026-11-26
evidence_library.finding: Inflammation drives COPD pathogenesis and exacerbations; exposure to cigarette smoke and other noxious particles produces a pathogenic triad (inflammation, protease-antiprotease imbalance, oxidative stress); oxidative stress from chronic smoking contributes to lung cellular damage, mucus hypersecretion and inflammation.
